requirement: Try named async sources in order, giving each a per-source timeout with asyncio.wait_for so a slow source is cancelled, return the first answer with its name, let non-timeout errors propagate, and raise TimeoutError when every source times out.
skeleton: first_within validating timeout and sources, then a loop awaiting asyncio.wait_for per source, continuing only on TimeoutError, and a final TimeoutError.
caption: Timeout fallback with the standard-library asyncio module. first_within(sources, timeout) takes a sequence of (name, zero-argument coroutine function) pairs and a timeout in seconds. It raises ValueError saying timeout must be positive when the timeout is zero or less, and ValueError saying at least one source is required for an empty sequence. For each source in order it awaits asyncio.wait_for on a fresh coroutine with that timeout and returns the name paired with the value. asyncio.wait_for cancels the slow coroutine and waits for the cancellation before raising TimeoutError, so the next source only starts after the previous one has stopped. Only TimeoutError moves on to the next source; any other exception, such as a RuntimeError from a broken database, propagates at once. When every source timed out it raises TimeoutError saying every source timed out. The fixture asserts that a one-second primary is cancelled before the cache fallback runs and the result is the cache pair, that a fast primary wins without calling the fallback, that a RuntimeError propagates instead of falling back, that two slow sources raise TimeoutError, and that a zero timeout and an empty list raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Serve a lookup from the first source that answers quickly
constraints: A non-positive timeout or empty source list raises ValueError
Each source gets its own timeout and is cancelled when it expires
Only timeouts fall through to the next source; other errors propagate
When every source times out, TimeoutError is raised

rationale.teaches: asyncio.wait_for as a per-attempt deadline that cancels the inner coroutine, with fallback restricted to TimeoutError.
rationale.why: Fallback code often catches every exception, shields the slow task so it keeps running, or stops after the first timeout, and a cancellation probe plus a raising source are needed to tell those apart.

ops.docstring: Bound slow async lookups with asyncio.wait_for and fall back to the next source.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence

candidates.why_wrong: RuntimeError is treated like a timeout, so a broken source is hidden behind the fallback.
The coroutine is shielded, so the slow source keeps running and is not cancelled before the fallback starts.
A zero timeout is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
An empty source list raises TimeoutError rather than ValueError.
The loop stops at the first timeout, so no fallback is ever tried.
